thread:
maya: Heads up — saw a request for tenant=acme go to the fallback route instead of the dedicated /acme route. Noticed this in the dashboard when debugging a customer alert.
sam: ugh. any decision log for that request? can you paste the eval trace?
maya: pasted a minimal reproducer below — header value sent is correct but the rule eval picked default-route.
maya: ```http
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
X-Tenant-Id: acme
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
```
maya: decision log excerpt:
maya: ```json
{"request_id":"r_123","route_evaluation":{"matched_rule":"default-route","evaluated_conditions":[{"cond":"headers.x-tenant-id == \"acme\"","result":false}],"sampling":false}}
```
jia: hmm. two quick possibilities: header normalization mismatch (we store headers lowercased as `x-tenant-id`) vs the rule engine expecting `headers.x-tenant-id` — but that normally works. second: sampling dropped the richer trace so we only got the sampled lightweight decision. `sampling":false` means we didn't keep the full decision log payload.
sam: so the rule engine evaluated it and concluded false — but why? maybe an intermediate proxy rewrote the header (X-Tenant-Id -> X-Tenant-Id: Acme) or added whitespace/casing differences.
maya: I inspected the raw ingress and it had `X-Tenant-Id: acme` lowercase value. I also saw an auth-proxy that sometimes injects `x-tenant` header. possible header alias collision.
jia: let's enable full decision logging for tenant "acme" for 15m and force sample=1.0 for any request with either header name `x-tenant-id` or `x-tenant` so we capture the full trace.
jia: you can flip this via the internal debug API (console -> Routing -> Debug flags) or curl:
jia: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://control.redwood.internal/debug/traces" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"selector":{"headers_any":["x-tenant-id","x-tenant"],"tenant":"acme"},"sampling":1.0,"duration_seconds":900}'
```
maya: doing that now.
deploy-bot: trace collection enabled for selector {tenant:acme, headers_any:[x-tenant-id,x-tenant]} (id:dbg_789) — will expire in 15m :white_check_mark:
sam: once we have a full trace we can see the exact header map handed to the route-evaluator and whether earlier stages transformed it.
maya: dbg_789 trace shows both headers present in some requests: `x-tenant-id: acme` and `x-tenant: acme\n` (note trailing newline on some requests) — that explains the boolean mismatch.
jia: trailing newline is killer. route condition does strict equality. two fixes: 1) normalize header values before eval (trim whitespace) 2) add a tolerant matcher e.g. `headers.x-tenant-id.trim().lower() == "acme"` if we support trim().
sam: prefer normalization at the ingress/proxy layer so all rules benefit. but add a defensive change in rule as quick rollback:
sam: - update rule to use `starts_with(headers.x-tenant-id, "acme")` or `regex_match` until we ship trimming.
maya: agreed — I'll open a tiny PR to add a header-normalizer middleware and also patch the /acme route rule to tolerate whitespace.
maya: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/normalize-tenant-header/pull/12
sam: ack, validate on staging with the debug trace turned on then roll.
jia: followups: (a) add a unit test to routing-eval that simulates header with trailing whitespace (b) add a health alert if fallback-route matches >0.1% of acme traffic in 5m.
maya: noted. i'll create tickets.
maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
sam: thanks — nice catch.
deploy-bot: debug trace dbg_789 expired (15m) — archived logs available at https://logs.redwood.internal/trace/dbg_789
maya: grabbed the archived trace, will attach to the PR.
sam: nice. closing loop once PR is merged and staging looks good.
